name: Synthwave
description: A microgenre of electronic music based predominantly on the music associated with action, science fiction, and horror film soundtracks of the 1980s.

name: Shoegaze
description: A subgenre of indie and alternative rock characterized by an ethereal mixture of obscured vocals, guitar distortion and effects, feedback, and overwhelming volume.

name: Afrobeats
description: An umbrella term to describe popular music from West Africa and the diaspora that blends West African musical styles with American funk, jazz, and contemporary dance music.

name: Lo-Fi Hip Hop
description: A subgenre of hip hop characterized by low-fidelity sound quality, relaxed tempos, and jazz chord progressions, heavily utilized for studying and relaxation.

name: Math Rock
description: A style of indie rock characterized by complex, atypical rhythmic structures, counterpoint, odd time signatures, and angular melodies.

name: Post-Punk
description: A rock music movement emerging in the late 1970s that departed from traditional punk rock by adopting avant-garde sensibilities and diverse influences like electronic and dub.

name: City Pop
description: A loose category of Japanese pop music that peaked in the late 1980s, heavily influenced by Western soft rock, R&B, funk, and boogie.

name: Hyperpop
description: A microgenre characterized by an exaggerated, high-energy, and self-referential take on pop music, heavily featuring pitched-up vocals and aggressive electronic production.

name: Bossa Nova
description: A style of Brazilian music developed and popularized in the late 1950s and 1960s, combining elements of samba and cool jazz with lyrical, syncopated acoustic guitar acoustic rhythms.

name: Drum and Bass
description: A genre of electronic dance music characterized by fast breakbeats (typically 160–180 beats per minute) with heavy bass and sub-bass lines.

name: Trip Hop
description: A genre of electronic music that originated in the early 1990s in the UK, blending slow-tempo hip hop beats with electronic, jazz, and psychedelic elements.

name: Gothic Rock
description: A subgenre of post-punk and alternative rock that emerged in the late 1970s, featuring dark, melancholic melodies, prominent basslines, and dramatic, baritone vocals.

name: Industrial
description: A genre of experimental music that draws on harsh, mechanical, and transgressive soundscapes, often incorporating electronic instrumentation and avant-garde themes.

name: Bluegrass
description: A genre of American roots music that developed in the 1940s in the Appalachian region, characterized by acoustic stringed instruments playing fast, improvised, polyphonic melodies.

name: Psychedelic Rock
description: A rock music style inspired or influenced by psychedelic culture, utilizing sound effects, distortion, tape loops, and long improvisational solos to replicate mind-altering experiences.

name: IDM (Intelligent Dance Music)
description: A subgenre of electronic music originating in the early 1990s, focused on individualistic experimentation and complex rhythmic patterns rather than standard dancefloor structures.

name: Eurodance
description: A genre of electronic dance music that originated in the late 1980s in Europe, combining elements of techno, hi-NRG, and house with prominent female vocals and male raps.

name: Dark Wave
description: A music movement that emerged from the new wave and post-punk movement of the late 1970s, incorporating dark, introspective lyrics and sorrowful undertones with synthesizers.

name: Ska
description: A music genre that originated in Jamaica in the late 1950s, combining Caribbean calypso and mento with American jazz and rhythm and blues, characterized by a walking bassline accented on the offbeat.

name: Ambiance / Ambient
description: A genre of music that emphasizes tone and atmosphere over traditional musical structure or rhythm, designed to evoke an atmospheric or visual quality.

name: Doom Metal
description: An extreme subgenre of heavy metal music that typically uses slower tempos, low-tuned guitars, and a much thicker or heavier sound to evoke a sense of despair and dread.

name: Glitch Hop
description: An electronic music genre that fuses the mid-tempo rhythms of hip hop with the jagged, digitized, and malfunctioning sound aesthetics of glitch music.

name: Reggaeton
description: A music genre that originated in Puerto Rico during the late 1990s, heavily influenced by hip hop, dancehall, and Latin American music, propelled by the 'Dem Bow' drum rhythm.

name: Dream Pop
description: A subgenre of alternative rock and neo-psychedelia that emphasizes atmosphere and sonic textures as much as melody, featuring breathy vocals and shimmering guitar work.

name: Phonk
description: A subgenre of hip hop and trap music directly inspired by 1990s Memphis rap, often characterized by distorted cowbells, chopped vocals, and heavy bass.

name: Gabba / Gabber
description: A style of electronic dance music and a subgenre of hardcore techno characterized by very fast, distorted, overdriven bass drum sounds, often reaching 150 to 190 BPM.

name: Garage Rock
description: A raw and energetic style of rock and roll that flourished in the mid-1960s, typically recorded by young, amateur bands playing basic chord progressions on fuzzy guitars.

name: Deep House
description: A subgenre of house music that originated in the 1980s, blending elements of Chicago house with jazz-funk, soul, and atmospheric, ambient pad sounds.

name: Nu-Metal
description: A subgenre of alternative metal that combines heavy metal guitar riffs with elements of other music genres such as hip hop, funk, grunge, and electronic music.

name: Chiptune
description: A style of synthesized electronic music made using the sound chips of vintage computers, video game consoles, and arcade machines.

name: Dubstep
description: A genre of electronic dance music that originated in South London in the late 1990s, marked by sparse, syncopated rhythmic patterns and prominent sub-bass frequencies.

name: Roots Reggae
description: A spiritual and socially conscious subgenre of reggae music that developed in Jamaica, dealing heavily with Rastafarian beliefs, poverty, and resistance to oppression.

name: Art Pop
description: A loosely defined pop music style influenced by art-school trends, avant-garde art, literature, and pop culture, prioritizing stylistic experimentation.

name: Hardstyle
description: An electronic dance music genre mixing influences from hard techno and hardcore, featuring a deeply distorted hardstyle kick drum, reversed basslines, and synth melodies.

name: Outlaw Country
description: A subgenre of country music that emerged in the late 1960s and 1970s as a reaction against the polished, commercial restrictions of the Nashville sound.

name: Flamenco
description: A highly expressive Spanish art form that includes cante (singing), toque (guitar playing), baile (dance), jaleo (vocalizations), and palmas (handclapping).

name: Techno
description: A form of electronic dance music that emerged in Detroit during the mid-to-late 1980s, characterized by a repetitive four-on-the-floor beat and futuristic aesthetic.

name: Hardcore Punk
description: An extreme, faster, and more aggressive subgenre of punk rock that originated in the late 1970s, featuring short, loud, and intense songs with socio-political lyrics.

name: G-Funk
description: A subgenre of gangsta rap that emerged from the West Coast hip hop scene in the early 1990s, characterized by slow, hypnotic funk grooves and high-pitched synthesizer portamentos.

name: Symphonic Metal
description: A subgenre of heavy metal that combines the aggressive drums and guitars of metal with the grandiose elements of classical orchestral music, operatic vocals, and choirs.
